transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (ZenPay Eng Lead), Liam Foster (ZenPay PM), Jordan Park (ZenPay DevOps)

Summary:
Quick SDK walkthrough for Redwood Python/TypeScript clients, auth patterns (API key, SSO mention), env setup, and next steps for POC benchmarking. Demo focused on quickstarts, streaming, and embeddings + console pointers.

Topics:
- Python and TypeScript SDK quickstarts
- Auth and env var setup (API keys vs SSO/SSO mis-transcript)
- Example flows: generation, streaming, embeddings
- Console for keys, routes, and cost dashboards
- POC bench plan and artifacts to share

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh — we got about 45 minutes, we'll go through the SDK quickstart and then leave time for questions, sound good?
[00:12] Maya (ZenPay): Yeah that works, thanks. Quick note, Jordan's on mute but he'll jump in for infra bits.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood): I'll start with the Python quickstart, and Alex will flip to the Console for where to create API keys.
[00:33] Alex (Redwood): Alright, if you go to the Console, you can create a scoped API key for the environment. We usually recommend a service account key for backend calls and SSO/SAML for admin access — sorry I said SSO twice, transcription or me —
[00:48] Liam (ZenPay): Quick question, for ZenPay we need tokenization and PCI patterns, can keys be scoped to not exfiltrate data?
[00:56] Priya (Redwood): Yes, you can restrict keys by route and set retention policies; also Dedicated gives data isolation. We'll share SOC2 and the compliance page.
[01:10] Jordan (ZenPay): Do you have a VPC connector for private deployments? We might need traffic egress control.
[01:18] Alex (Redwood): Yep, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and on-prem packages — Priya can go over network options in the POC.
[01:27] Priya (Redwood): Jumping into code. Python: pip install redwood-sdk (note: sample package name used in quickstart; actual package may be redwood-inference-sdk). Example: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) — then call client.generate(...) for text.
[01:52] Priya (Redwood): For TypeScript: npm i @redwood/inference, import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); client.chat.create({ model: 'rwd-2-small', input: '...' }) — this is a quick pattern.
[02:15] Maya (ZenPay): Do you support streaming with the SDKs? Our UX needs token-by-token render.
[02:22] Priya (Redwood): Yes, both SDKs have streaming methods — in Python you can iterate over client.stream_generate, in TS there's an onDelta callback. Latency is influenced by batching and prefix caching.
[02:36] Speaker 1 (maybe Alex): Also, for embeddings, we have a embeddings endpoint; you can upsert to your vector DB. We'll share the sample integration for Pinecone/Weaviate.
[02:50] Liam (ZenPay): For auth, is it strictly API key or can we use SAML-based provisioning?
[02:58] Alex (Redwood): You can provision service keys via the Console and integrate SSO for user provisioning. For programmatic access we recommend short-lived keys and KMS integration for key rotation.
[03:12] Priya (Redwood): Quick demo: I'll paste a Python snippet that streams a small completion — console shows the request trace and per-token cost in the dashboard.
[03:28] Priya (Redwood): (typing) def stream_demo(): for chunk in client.stream_generate(...): print(chunk.text) — you'll see examples in the quickstart repo.
[03:45] Maya (ZenPay): Are there rate limits? We have bursty traffic at checkout.
[03:52] Priya (Redwood): Hosted has rate limits and we can set higher quotas for Dedicated; we can also configure autoscale and burst capacity. For strict SLAs, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[04:05] Jordan (ZenPay): Can the SDK pick model variants automatically for latency vs cost?
[04:12] Alex (Redwood): Yes, via routing policies you can prefer lower-cost variants and fallback to higher capacity models. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching profiles per workload.
[04:26] Liam (ZenPay): For the POC, we want to run a 24-hour baseline against our sample prompts — can you provide bench scripts?
[04:33] Priya (Redwood): We'll provide a bench script (Python) that simulates your percentiles and logs latency and tokens; I'll add quantized vs float32 runs.
[04:44] Alex (Redwood): We'll also include an example of streaming + reconciled cost per token in the Console so your finance folks can see unit economics.
[04:55] Maya (ZenPay): On embeddings, how do you handle freshness and upserts?
[05:02] Priya (Redwood): We expose an embeddings endpoint and you control vector indexing; we recommend batching updates and using the Optimize tool to suggest model sizes and dims.
[05:15] Speaker 2 (customer): Sorry small crosstalk, are there sample env files?
[05:20] Priya (Redwood): Yes, quickstart repo has .env.example showing REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV. For Dedicated you'll get a different base URL and creds.
[05:33] Liam (ZenPay): Any gotchas for TypeScript and bundlers?
[05:38] Priya (Redwood): We publish ESM and CJS builds — if you use edge workers, we have a lightweight fetch-based client. We'll send notes on bundler configs.
[05:50] Maya (ZenPay): Performance question: our 95th pct prompt length is about 1k tokens, how does that impact latency?
[05:58] Alex (Redwood): Sequence length affects kernel selection. Our runtime picks optimized kernels based on seq len distribution; larger sequences increase per-token time but batching and KV cache can help for chat flows.
[06:12] Priya (Redwood): For the demo portion, I'm going to share the quickstart repo link in chat now — sorry if the link text is a bit mangled by the transcript.
[06:22] Priya (Redwood): (paste) https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/tree/main/sdk -> Python and TypeScript folders.
[06:30] Maya (ZenPay): Got it. We'll review. Can you also share security docs and your SOC2 attestation?
[06:36] Alex (Redwood): Yes, we'll attach SOC2, ISO docs, and the VPC checklist to the CRM.
[06:44] Liam (ZenPay): How do we provision test keys for the POC? We need isolated environment and usage caps.
[06:51] Alex (Redwood): We can spin a tenant in Dedicated eval with scoped keys; for hosted we can create a billing-limited key. We'll follow up with instructions.
[07:02] Jordan (ZenPay): Network egress is a blocker until security signs off. What's the typical network architecture for Private?
[07:09] Priya (Redwood): For Private we offer an on-prem bundle or VPC peering with private IPs; we provide firewall rules and audit logs. We'll send the architecture diagram.
[07:22] Maya (ZenPay): Any final notes on SDK usage patterns?
[07:26] Priya (Redwood): Use short-lived keys, stream for UX, cache prefixes where possible, and run Optimize to get batching and quantization recommendations.
[07:36] Alex (Redwood): Recap of next steps: we'll share quickstarts, SOC2 and network docs, bench script, and schedule POC kickoff — does that capture it?
[07:45] Maya (ZenPay): Yes, sounds good. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
